questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Why Danish food is so popular
How the UN measures income and health
Small things we can do to feel happier
Why the pandemic has made everyone unhappy
questions.why: Neil says there are small things we can do to feel better about life, and happiness is the subject.

questions.q: What does Neil mean when he says Georgina sees 'the glass half full'?
options: She generally looks at things in a positive way
She is thirsty and always wants more to drink
She never quite finishes her work on time
She worries a lot about small, unimportant things
questions.why: He explains it means she generally looks at things in a positive way.

questions.q: Why does Georgina say it's important to discuss happiness now?
options: Because Denmark has a new book about it
Because the UN asked people to
Because people are richer than before
Because it matters more in a pandemic
questions.why: She says it may seem strange during a pandemic, but right now feeling happy is more important than ever.

questions.q: What does Malene Rydahl say we should focus on for happiness?
options: Earning more money
The quality of our relationships
Travelling to new countries
Comparing ourselves with others
questions.why: She says 'what we need to focus on is the quality of our relationships'.

questions.q: What daily habit does Malene Rydahl recommend?
options: Sleeping for at least eight hours every night
Drinking hot coffee
Finding three things to be grateful for
Writing down your goals
questions.why: Georgina says she recommends finding three things to be grateful for every day.

questions.q: According to Malene Rydahl, what happens if you confuse happiness with pleasure?
options: You become more beautiful and confident
You keep chasing more but are never satisfied
You become very successful in your career
You stop caring about other people around you
questions.why: She says you'll be like a hamster in a wheel because it's never enough.

questions.q: What is the 'hedonic treadmill', as Georgina explains it?
options: We adapt, so getting more never satisfies us
A machine that helps people exercise
A way of saving money for the future
The feeling of joy after a big success
questions.why: She says as we get what we desire our expectations also increase, so we never find the happiness we hoped for.

questions.q: Why does Neil mention his grandma?
options: She lived in Denmark, the happiest country
She was always happy, even when she was poor
She taught him to be grateful for small things
She used to say that money can't buy happiness
questions.why: Neil says 'Money can't buy happiness', as my grandma used to say.
